code_snippets.title: Audit log row (append-only)
code_snippets.code:
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone


def audit_row(user_id: str, tool: str, args: dict, status: str) -> dict:
    payload = json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True)
    return {
        "user_id": user_id,
        "tool": tool,
        "args_hash": hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()[:16],
        "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "status": status,
    }

code_snippets.title: Audit log row (append-only)
code_snippets.code:
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone


def audit_row(user_id: str, tool: str, args: dict, status: str) -> dict:
    payload = json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True)
    return {
        "user_id": user_id,
        "tool": tool,
        "args_hash": hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()[:16],
        "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "status": status,
    }

# MCP introduction

> **Visual study guide** · Course 3 · Read · [modelcontextprotocol.io ↗](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction)

## Problem MCP solves

Agents need **tools** (query warehouse, run job, read ticket). Without a standard, every host invents its own plugin format. **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** defines how a **host** discovers and calls **tools** on a **server**—with schemas, auth boundaries, and audit-friendly requests.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Host["MCP host (Cursor, Claude Desktop, your agent)"]
    H[Orchestrator]
  end
  subgraph Server["MCP server (your service)"]
    T1[tool: run_query]
    T2[tool: fetch_schema]
    R[resources / prompts]
  end
  H <-->|JSON-RPC transport| Server
```

## Roles (memorize these)

| Role | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| **Host** | User session, model, when to call tools |
| **Client** | Connection from host to server (often embedded in host) |
| **Server** | Exposes tools/resources; enforces authz |

You will **build servers** and **consume** them from LangGraph nodes—not reimplement MCP inside every tool.

## Request lifecycle

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Host
  participant Server
  Host->>Server: initialize / list_tools
  Server-->>Host: tool schemas JSON Schema
  Host->>Server: call_tool(name, args)
  Server-->>Host: structured result or error
  Note over Server: Log caller tool args hash outcome
```

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  AG[Agent / LangGraph node]
  MCP[MCP server]
  AUD[(Audit log)]
  SEC[Secrets via SM / env]
  DATA[(Warehouse read-only role)]
  AG --> MCP
  MCP --> AUD
  MCP --> SEC
  MCP --> DATA
```

de_lab.scenario_title: Audited tools instead of ad-hoc SQL in prompts
de_lab.scenario_markdown:
An agent must **look up schema metadata** and **run read-only queries** against a staging schema—not arbitrary warehouse admin. Expose tools via **MCP** with JSON Schema, log every call (`user_id`, `tool`, `args_hash`, `timestamp`, `status`). This mirrors stored procedures + query audit tables you already use for compliance.

**Tools to implement:** `lookup_schema`, `query_golden_set`, `run_readonly_sql` (allow-listed tables only).

code_snippets.title: Audit log row (append-only)
code_snippets.code:
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone


def audit_row(user_id: str, tool: str, args: dict, status: str) -> dict:
    payload = json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True)
    return {
        "user_id": user_id,
        "tool": tool,
        "args_hash": hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()[:16],
        "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "status": status,
    }

de_lab.scenario_title: Audited tools instead of ad-hoc SQL in prompts
de_lab.scenario_markdown:
An agent must **look up schema metadata** and **run read-only queries** against a staging schema—not arbitrary warehouse admin. Expose tools via **MCP** with JSON Schema, log every call (`user_id`, `tool`, `args_hash`, `timestamp`, `status`). This mirrors stored procedures + query audit tables you already use for compliance.

**Tools to implement:** `lookup_schema`, `query_golden_set`, `run_readonly_sql` (allow-listed tables only).

code_snippets.title: Audit log row (append-only)
code_snippets.code:
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone


def audit_row(user_id: str, tool: str, args: dict, status: str) -> dict:
    payload = json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True)
    return {
        "user_id": user_id,
        "tool": tool,
        "args_hash": hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()[:16],
        "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "status": status,
    }

de_lab.scenario_markdown:
An agent must **look up schema metadata** and **run read-only queries** against a staging schema—not arbitrary warehouse admin. Expose tools via **MCP** with JSON Schema, log every call (`user_id`, `tool`, `args_hash`, `timestamp`, `status`). This mirrors stored procedures + query audit tables you already use for compliance.

code_snippets.title: Audit log row (append-only)
code_snippets.code:
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone


def audit_row(user_id: str, tool: str, args: dict, status: str) -> dict:
    payload = json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True)
    return {
        "user_id": user_id,
        "tool": tool,
        "args_hash": hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()[:16],
        "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "status": status,
    }

code_snippets.title: Audit log row (append-only)
code_snippets.code:
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone


def audit_row(user_id: str, tool: str, args: dict, status: str) -> dict:
    payload = json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True)
    return {
        "user_id": user_id,
        "tool": tool,
        "args_hash": hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()[:16],
        "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "status": status,
    }

de_lab.scenario_title: Audited tools instead of ad-hoc SQL in prompts
de_lab.scenario_markdown:
An agent must **look up schema metadata** and **run read-only queries** against a staging schema—not arbitrary warehouse admin. Expose tools via **MCP** with JSON Schema, log every call (`user_id`, `tool`, `args_hash`, `timestamp`, `status`). This mirrors stored procedures + query audit tables you already use for compliance.

**Tools to implement:** `lookup_schema`, `query_golden_set`, `run_readonly_sql` (allow-listed tables only).

code_snippets.title: Audit log row (append-only)
code_snippets.code:
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone


def audit_row(user_id: str, tool: str, args: dict, status: str) -> dict:
    payload = json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True)
    return {
        "user_id": user_id,
        "tool": tool,
        "args_hash": hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()[:16],
        "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "status": status,
    }

# Document Chat RAG walkthrough

> **Visual study guide** · Course 4 · Video · [YouTube walkthrough ↗](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zgnjMWipirk)

## What RAG is (one sentence)

**Retrieval-augmented generation**: fetch relevant chunks from a corpus, inject them into the prompt, then ask the model to answer **grounded in those chunks**—not from parametric memory alone.

Data-engineering analogy: **join to a reference table** before computing a metric.

## End-to-end RAG pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  DOC[Documents PDF MD logs]
  CHUNK[Chunking strategy]
  EMB[Embedding model]
  VDB[(Vector store e.g. pgvector)]
  Q[User query]
  RET[Top-k retrieval]
  PROMPT[Augmented prompt]
  LLM[LLM]
  ANS[Answer + citations]

  DOC --> CHUNK --> EMB --> VDB
  Q --> EMB --> RET
  VDB --> RET --> PROMPT --> LLM --> ANS
```

## Chunking is a data modeling choice

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Strategies["Common strategies"]
    FIX[Fixed token windows]
    SEC[Section / heading aware]
    REC[Recursive split]
  end
  FIX --> TRADE[Recall vs precision tradeoff]
  SEC --> TRADE
  REC --> TRADE
```

| Strategy | Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fixed size | Simple | Splits tables / code badly |
| Heading-aware | Better docs | Needs structure metadata |
| Overlap windows | Higher recall | More storage & cost |

## Retrieval quality levers

- **Embedding model** — domain fit beats random OpenAI default for specialized logs.
- **k** — too few misses context; too many dilutes prompt.
- **Metadata filters** — tenant, date, source system (like partition pruning).
- **Hybrid** — BM25 + vectors for keyword-heavy queries (Month 4+ reads).

## Grounding and hallucination

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant User
  participant RAG
  participant Store
  User->>RAG: question
  RAG->>Store: similarity search
  Store-->>RAG: chunks + scores
  RAG->>RAG: build prompt with citations
  Note over RAG: If chunks empty refuse or escalate
  RAG-->>User: answer citing chunk ids
```

**Fail closed** when retrieval returns nothing relevant—do not let the model freestyle.

## While you watch

- [ ] Note **chunk size** and **overlap** used in the demo.
- [ ] Identify where **embeddings** are created vs queried.
- [ ] List what you would log: query, k, chunk ids, scores, model id.
- [ ] Sketch how pgvector fits your capstone (table DDL, index).

## Connect to pgvector prove (next reads)

```mermaid
erDiagram
  DOCUMENTS ||--o{ CHUNKS : contains
  CHUNKS {
    uuid id
    vector embedding
    text content
    jsonb metadata
  }
```

## Failure modes

| Issue | Signal | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stale index | Wrong doc version answers | Version source docs; re-embed on change |
| Chunk too large | Truncated context | Smaller chunks + parent retrieval |
| No citations | Untraceable answers | Require chunk ids in output schema |
| Injection via docs | Malicious corpus text | Sanitize sources; separate trust zones |

## Done when

You can draw **ingest → chunk → embed → store → retrieve → prompt → answer** and name one metric you will use in Month 7 eval (e.g. context precision).

## Primary source

[Document Chat RAG walkthrough ↗](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zgnjMWipirk) — then implement the pattern in your repo with **pgvector** per Course 4 build/prove items.

## Architecture (visual)

Boundaries, failure paths, and stores—not a generic pipeline sticker.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Q[Question] --> EMB[Embedding]
  Q --> BM25[Lexical sparse]
  EMB --> RRF[RRF fusion]
  BM25 --> RRF
  RRF --> TOPK[Top-k chunks]
  TOPK --> EVAL[recall@k vs labels]
```

## Request flow (sequence)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Client
  participant Platform as Your service
  participant Dep as External dependency
  Client->>Platform: request
  Platform->>Dep: bounded call
  Dep-->>Platform: response
  Platform-->>Client: validated output
```

digest.title: Hybrid Search: Lexical (BM25) + Dense Neural Embeddings
takeaways: Dense vector search alone fails on exact keyword matches (part numbers, IDs, specialized jargon, acronyms).
Hybrid search combines sparse lexical BM25 retrieval with dense cosine similarity for maximum recall.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) merges ranked candidate lists without needing score normalization.
rules: Calculate RRF Score: RRF(d) = sum(1 / (k + rank_i(d))) where k=60.
Pass top 50 candidates from hybrid retrieval through a neural Cross-Encoder reranker (Cohere / BGE-Reranker) to select top 5.
Chunk documents based on semantic markdown boundaries rather than arbitrary character splits.
pitfalls: Relying solely on dense embeddings for domain-specific technical documentation.
Skipping the reranking step, which accounts for 15-25% improvement in context precision.

code_snippets.title: Example validator query (Neo4j)
code_snippets.code:
MATCH (a:Account)-[:HAS_EVENT]->(e:Event)
WITH a, sum(e.amount_usd) AS total
WHERE abs(total) > 0.01
RETURN a.id AS account_id, total

code_snippets.title: Example validator query (Neo4j)
code_snippets.code:
MATCH (a:Account)-[:HAS_EVENT]->(e:Event)
WITH a, sum(e.amount_usd) AS total
WHERE abs(total) > 0.01
RETURN a.id AS account_id, total

code_snippets.title: CI workflow stub
code_snippets.code:
name: eval-gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  evals:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      - run: python -m evals.run --fail-on-regression

- **Audit log** — Append-only record of who invoked which tool with what outcome.
  - *Data pipeline analogy:* CloudTrail / data access logs for compliance.
- **Golden set** — Fixed labeled examples (input → expected output) used to score changes.
  - *Data pipeline analogy:* Fixture tables in dbt tests or regression datasets.

| Golden set | Fixed labeled examples (input → expected output) used to score changes. | Fixture tables in dbt tests or regression datasets. |
| RAG | Retrieval-augmented generation: fetch relevant docs, then answer with the model. | Join to a reference table before computing a metric. |

## Lab & Practice

**DE lens:** Ship a measurable artifact in your portfolio repo; prove with tests or benchmarks.

### Real-world placement

After single-model extraction works, production needs failover—not a 3am pages for 429s.

### What you implement

Add `policy/analyst.rego` denying `write_*` tools and `tests/test_policy.sh` with `opa test policy/ -v`.

### Expected outcome

README shows one forced failure switching to fallback successfully.

### Starter code (adapt paths)

```python
# gateway/gateway.py
import hashlib
import json
import time
from tenacity import retry, retry_if_exception, stop_after_attempt, wait_exponential
from litellm import completion
from litellm.exceptions import RateLimitError

def _prompt_hash(messages: list[dict]) -> str:
    blob = json.dumps(messages, sort_keys=True).encode()
    return hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest()[:16]

@retry(
    retry=retry_if_exception(lambda e: isinstance(e, RateLimitError)),
    wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=1, min=1, max=30),
    stop=stop_after_attempt(3),
)
def complete(job_id: str, messages: list[dict]) -> dict:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    resp = completion(model="gpt-4o-mini", messages=messages, metadata={"job_id": job_id})
    row = {
        "job_id": job_id,
        "prompt_hash": _prompt_hash(messages),
        "model": resp.model,
        "prompt_tokens": resp.usage.prompt_tokens,
        "completion_tokens": resp.usage.completion_tokens,
        "latency_ms": int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000),
    }
    with open("logs/usage.jsonl", "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
    return row
```

**Primary source:** [LiteLLM — Langfuse integration](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/observability/langfuse_integration)

# LiteLLM — Langfuse integration

> **Platform depth** — engineering judgment: tradeoffs, metrics, failures, interviews. Read **Study guide** first if you have not done the checklist.

## Platform narrative (this topic)

LiteLLM is the **control plane** for model routing: budgets, fallbacks, and uniform logging. Design for **multi-tenant** use even in a solo repo—per-request metadata (job_id, pipeline, tenant) must flow into logs for cost chargeback. Alert on fallback rate spikes; they often indicate quality or availability regression, not healthy resilience.

## How this topic fits the month’s architecture

- Langfuse traces and run_id correlation
- OPA allow/deny on tools
- Redaction before sharing traces

## Primary source focus

- Reliable completions
- Fallbacks
- Timeouts

## Failure modes to design for

- Fallback model serves 100% of traffic silently—quality drifts undetected.
- 429 storms without client-side backoff take down the worker pool.
- Prompt+response logged with PII for debugging.

## Metrics and alerts

- `usd_per_request_p99`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `latency_ms_p99`

- Alert: fallback_rate > 5% over 15m

- Alert: validation_error_rate spike vs 7d baseline

## Tradeoffs (explicit)

| Option | Upside | Downside |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Central LiteLLM proxy | Uniform logs, budgets, fallbacks | Single point of failure; needs HA |
| Per-service API keys | Team velocity | No cost attribution; secret sprawl |

## Decision record (fill before you ship)

| Stance | Your choice | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adopt now | … | Why LiteLLM — Langfuse integration is in scope this month |
| Experiment | … | What you will measure in two weeks |
| Defer | … | What risk you accept by waiting |

## Interview depth

- Draw a box diagram: where does **LiteLLM — Langfuse integration** sit between data landing and warehouse load?
- What is your rollback plan if a model upgrade drops golden-set pass rate by 5%?
- How do you prove schema validity ≠ semantic correctness with one example?
- How do you allocate model budget per team without shared API keys?
- When is fallback worse than failing fast?

## Capstone implementation

Configure primary + fallback model list; log which model served each request.

## Advanced done bar

README shows one forced failure switching to fallback successfully.

## Prove bar

- OPA test or policy unit test
- Langfuse/OTel trace screenshot with run_id

## Production notes (still plain English)

Before changing models or prompts in production, re-check the course **prove pack** and golden-set metrics (cost, latency, valid JSON %).


### Platform depth addendum

Re-read rollout and failure-mode sections with gateway metrics and golden-set labels open. Staff reviewers expect explicit tradeoffs on cost, latency, schema strictness, and audit—not a lecture recap.

lab_practice.markdown:
## Lab & Practice

**DE lens:** Ship a measurable artifact in your portfolio repo; prove with tests or benchmarks.

### Real-world placement

After single-model extraction works, production needs failover—not a 3am pages for 429s.

### What you implement

Create `gateway/gateway.py` wrapping `litellm.completion` with Tenacity retries on HTTP 429 (exponential backoff, max 3), logging `prompt_hash` (sha256 of system+user), `model`, tokens, and `latency_ms` to `logs/usage.jsonl`.

### Expected outcome

README shows one forced failure switching to fallback successfully.

### Starter code (adapt paths)

```python
# gateway/gateway.py
import hashlib
import json
import time
from tenacity import retry, retry_if_exception, stop_after_attempt, wait_exponential
from litellm import completion
from litellm.exceptions import RateLimitError

def _prompt_hash(messages: list[dict]) -> str:
    blob = json.dumps(messages, sort_keys=True).encode()
    return hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest()[:16]

@retry(
    retry=retry_if_exception(lambda e: isinstance(e, RateLimitError)),
    wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=1, min=1, max=30),
    stop=stop_after_attempt(3),
)
def complete(job_id: str, messages: list[dict]) -> dict:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    resp = completion(model="gpt-4o-mini", messages=messages, metadata={"job_id": job_id})
    row = {
        "job_id": job_id,
        "prompt_hash": _prompt_hash(messages),
        "model": resp.model,
        "prompt_tokens": resp.usage.prompt_tokens,
        "completion_tokens": resp.usage.completion_tokens,
        "latency_ms": int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000),
    }
    with open("logs/usage.jsonl", "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
    return row
```

# Langfuse wired to LangGraph + LiteLLM

> **Platform depth** — engineering judgment: tradeoffs, metrics, failures, interviews. Read **Study guide** first if you have not done the checklist.

## Platform narrative (this topic)

LiteLLM is the **control plane** for model routing: budgets, fallbacks, and uniform logging. Design for **multi-tenant** use even in a solo repo—per-request metadata (job_id, pipeline, tenant) must flow into logs for cost chargeback. Alert on fallback rate spikes; they often indicate quality or availability regression, not healthy resilience.

## How this topic fits the month’s architecture

- Langfuse traces and run_id correlation
- OPA allow/deny on tools
- Redaction before sharing traces

## Primary source focus

- Reliable completions
- Fallbacks
- Timeouts

## Failure modes to design for

- Fallback model serves 100% of traffic silently—quality drifts undetected.
- 429 storms without client-side backoff take down the worker pool.
- Prompt+response logged with PII for debugging.

## Metrics and alerts

- `usd_per_request_p99`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `latency_ms_p99`

- Alert: fallback_rate > 5% over 15m

- Alert: validation_error_rate spike vs 7d baseline

## Tradeoffs (explicit)

| Option | Upside | Downside |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Central LiteLLM proxy | Uniform logs, budgets, fallbacks | Single point of failure; needs HA |
| Per-service API keys | Team velocity | No cost attribution; secret sprawl |

## Decision record (fill before you ship)

| Stance | Your choice | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adopt now | … | Why Langfuse wired to LangGraph + LiteLLM is in scope this month |
| Experiment | … | What you will measure in two weeks |
| Defer | … | What risk you accept by waiting |

## Interview depth

- Draw a box diagram: where does **Langfuse wired to LangGraph + LiteLLM** sit between data landing and warehouse load?
- What is your rollback plan if a model upgrade drops golden-set pass rate by 5%?
- How do you prove schema validity ≠ semantic correctness with one example?
- How do you allocate model budget per team without shared API keys?
- When is fallback worse than failing fast?

lab_practice.markdown:
## Lab & Practice

**DE lens:** Ship a measurable artifact in your portfolio repo; prove with tests or benchmarks.

### Real-world placement

After single-model extraction works, production needs failover—not a 3am pages for 429s.

### What you implement

Create `gateway/gateway.py` wrapping `litellm.completion` with Tenacity retries on HTTP 429 (exponential backoff, max 3), logging `prompt_hash` (sha256 of system+user), `model`, tokens, and `latency_ms` to `logs/usage.jsonl`.

### Expected outcome

README shows one forced failure switching to fallback successfully.

### Starter code (adapt paths)

```python
# gateway/gateway.py
import hashlib
import json
import time
from tenacity import retry, retry_if_exception, stop_after_attempt, wait_exponential
from litellm import completion
from litellm.exceptions import RateLimitError

def _prompt_hash(messages: list[dict]) -> str:
    blob = json.dumps(messages, sort_keys=True).encode()
    return hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest()[:16]

@retry(
    retry=retry_if_exception(lambda e: isinstance(e, RateLimitError)),
    wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=1, min=1, max=30),
    stop=stop_after_attempt(3),
)
def complete(job_id: str, messages: list[dict]) -> dict:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    resp = completion(model="gpt-4o-mini", messages=messages, metadata={"job_id": job_id})
    row = {
        "job_id": job_id,
        "prompt_hash": _prompt_hash(messages),
        "model": resp.model,
        "prompt_tokens": resp.usage.prompt_tokens,
        "completion_tokens": resp.usage.completion_tokens,
        "latency_ms": int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000),
    }
    with open("logs/usage.jsonl", "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
    return row
```

## Lab & Practice

**DE lens:** Ship a measurable artifact in your portfolio repo; prove with tests or benchmarks.

### Real-world placement

Boot week: your reconciler must return typed JSON, not free-form text.

### What you implement

Implement `extractor/extract.py` with `instructor.from_openai`, `response_model=LogEvent`, `max_retries=3`, and structured log on each `ValidationError` including field path.

### Expected outcome

Golden set reports valid JSON % on `data/golden/`.

### Starter code (adapt paths)

```python
# extract_one.py — wire to your golden set
from pydantic import BaseModel
import instructor
from openai import OpenAI

class LogEvent(BaseModel):
    event_id: str
    severity: str
    message: str

client = instructor.from_openai(OpenAI())

def extract(raw: str) -> LogEvent:
    return client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o-mini",
        response_model=LogEvent,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": raw}],
        max_retries=3,
    )
```

## Lab & Practice

**DE lens:** Ship a measurable artifact in your portfolio repo; prove with tests or benchmarks.

### Real-world placement

Course 2 wraps your reconciler in a graph with HITL on validation failure.

### What you implement

Compile `reconciler_agent/graph.py` with `SqliteSaver` checkpointer, `interrupt_before=['commit']`, and pytest that feeds invalid parsed JSON and expects graph pause state.

README GIF or steps: fail → interrupt → human fix → resume.

### Starter code (adapt paths)

```python
# graph.py — add checkpoint + interrupt on validation error
from langgraph.types import interrupt

def validate(state):
    if state.get("errors"):
        interrupt({"errors": state["errors"]})
    return state
```

### 3. Core concepts

- **TTFT** — Time to first token—latency until the model starts streaming output. _DE angle:_ Time-to-first-byte on an API response.
- **Audit log** — Append-only record of who invoked which tool with what outcome. _DE angle:_ CloudTrail / data access logs for compliance.
- **Golden set** — Fixed labeled examples (input → expected output) used to score changes. _DE angle:_ Fixture tables in dbt tests or regression datasets.
- **RAG** — Retrieval-augmented generation: fetch relevant docs, then answer with the model. _DE angle:_ Join to a reference table before computing a metric.
- **Embedding** — Vector representation of text used for similarity search. _DE angle:_ Feature vector for fuzzy matching instead of exact keys.
- **Tool schema** — JSON schema describing parameters an agent tool accepts. _DE angle:_ API request body contract.
- **MCP** — Model Context Protocol—standard way to expose tools and resources to models. _DE angle:_ Internal tool catalog + OpenAPI for agents.
- **Sampling** — How the model picks the next token (temperature, top-p). _DE angle:_ Random seed / tie-break policy—lower temperature = more deterministic.
- **Agent** — System that plans steps and calls tools; not just one LLM prompt. _DE angle:_ Orchestrated micro-jobs with side effects—not a single SQL statement.
- **Eval harness** — Scripts/CI that run the golden set and report metrics on every change. _DE angle:_ pytest + data diff job in CI.
- **LLM gateway** — Central entry for models: auth, routing, budgets, logging, fallbacks. _DE angle:_ Kong/Apigee-style layer before downstream services.
- **Structured output** — Forcing LLM responses into a schema (JSON/Pydantic) instead of free text. _DE angle:_ Contract-first API response types and schema enforcement.

lab_practice.title: Lab & Practice
lab_practice.markdown:
## Lab & Practice

**DE lens:** Ship a measurable artifact in your portfolio repo; prove with tests or benchmarks.

### Real-world placement

After single-model extraction works, production needs failover—not a 3am pages for 429s.

### What you implement

Create `gateway/gateway.py` wrapping `litellm.completion` with Tenacity retries on HTTP 429 (exponential backoff, max 3), logging `prompt_hash` (sha256 of system+user), `model`, tokens, and `latency_ms` to `logs/usage.jsonl`.

### Expected outcome

README shows one forced failure switching to fallback successfully.

### Starter code (adapt paths)

```python
# gateway/gateway.py
import hashlib
import json
import time
from tenacity import retry, retry_if_exception, stop_after_attempt, wait_exponential
from litellm import completion
from litellm.exceptions import RateLimitError

def _prompt_hash(messages: list[dict]) -> str:
    blob = json.dumps(messages, sort_keys=True).encode()
    return hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest()[:16]

@retry(
    retry=retry_if_exception(lambda e: isinstance(e, RateLimitError)),
    wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=1, min=1, max=30),
    stop=stop_after_attempt(3),
)
def complete(job_id: str, messages: list[dict]) -> dict:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    resp = completion(model="gpt-4o-mini", messages=messages, metadata={"job_id": job_id})
    row = {
        "job_id": job_id,
        "prompt_hash": _prompt_hash(messages),
        "model": resp.model,
        "prompt_tokens": resp.usage.prompt_tokens,
        "completion_tokens": resp.usage.completion_tokens,
        "latency_ms": int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000),
    }
    with open("logs/usage.jsonl", "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
    return row
```

**Primary source:** [LiteLLM prompt caching](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/prompt_caching)

> **Platform depth** — engineering judgment: tradeoffs, metrics, failures, interviews. Read **Study guide** first if you have not done the checklist.

## Platform narrative (this topic)

LiteLLM is the **control plane** for model routing: budgets, fallbacks, and uniform logging. Design for **multi-tenant** use even in a solo repo—per-request metadata (job_id, pipeline, tenant) must flow into logs for cost chargeback. Alert on fallback rate spikes; they often indicate quality or availability regression, not healthy resilience.

## How this topic fits the month’s architecture

- Prompt caching evidence table
- Eight capstone layers integrated
- OpenAPI surface for tools

## Primary source focus

- Reliable completions
- Fallbacks
- Timeouts

## Failure modes to design for

- Fallback model serves 100% of traffic silently—quality drifts undetected.
- 429 storms without client-side backoff take down the worker pool.
- Prompt+response logged with PII for debugging.

## Metrics and alerts

- `usd_per_request_p99`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `latency_ms_p99`

- Alert: fallback_rate > 5% over 15m

- Alert: validation_error_rate spike vs 7d baseline

| --- | --- | --- |
| Central LiteLLM proxy | Uniform logs, budgets, fallbacks | Single point of failure; needs HA |

## Lab & Practice

**DE lens:** Ship a measurable artifact in your portfolio repo; prove with tests or benchmarks.

### Real-world placement

Boot week: your reconciler must return typed JSON, not free-form text.

### What you implement

Implement `extractor/extract.py` with `instructor.from_openai`, `response_model=LogEvent`, `max_retries=3`, and structured log on each `ValidationError` including field path.

### Expected outcome

Golden set reports valid JSON % on `data/golden/`.

### Starter code (adapt paths)

```python
# extract_one.py — wire to your golden set
from pydantic import BaseModel
import instructor
from openai import OpenAI

class LogEvent(BaseModel):
    event_id: str
    severity: str
    message: str

client = instructor.from_openai(OpenAI())

def extract(raw: str) -> LogEvent:
    return client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o-mini",
        response_model=LogEvent,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": raw}],
        max_retries=3,
    )
```

**Primary source:** [Instructor](https://python.useinstructor.com/getting-started/)

> **Platform depth** — engineering judgment: tradeoffs, metrics, failures, interviews. Read **Study guide** first if you have not done the checklist.

## Platform narrative (this topic)

Instructor is your **adapter** between probabilistic text and deterministic types. Platform pattern: wrap `completion` in a function with `max_retries`, cap token spend per record, and emit structured logs on each `ValidationError`. Pair with a golden set where **semantic** errors (wrong amount) are labeled separately from **schema** errors.

## How this topic fits the month’s architecture

- Eight capstone layers integrated
- Prompt caching evidence table
- OpenAPI surface for tools

## Primary source focus

- Quick start
- Retries
- Partial validation

## Failure modes to design for

- Retries exhaust budget on systematically bad prompts.
- JSON parses but business invariants fail (silent wrong totals).
- Schema loosened in prod to ‘stop alerts’ without versioning.

## Metrics and alerts

- Task success rate on golden set (tier 1)

- Schema validation pass rate (tier 0)

- Cost per 1k successful extractions

| Option | Upside | Downside |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retry on ValidationError | Higher pass rate | Cost/latency multiply |
| Low temperature + no retry | Cheaper, stable | May under-recover on hard rows |

> **Platform depth** — engineering judgment: tradeoffs, metrics, failures, interviews. Read **Study guide** first if you have not done the checklist.

## Platform narrative (this topic)

LangGraph models **long-running work** with explicit state. Compare to Airflow: checkpoints are your idempotency keys; interrupts are human approval tasks. Size state payloads; large JSON in graph memory is an ops incident waiting to happen. Define SLAs for HITL steps.

## How this topic fits the month’s architecture

- Eight capstone layers integrated
- Prompt caching evidence table
- OpenAPI surface for tools

## Primary source focus

- Concepts
- Persistence
- Interrupts

## Failure modes to design for

- Fallback model serves 100% of traffic silently—quality drifts undetected.
- 429 storms without client-side backoff take down the worker pool.
- Prompt+response logged with PII for debugging.

## Metrics and alerts

- `graph_step_latency_p99`, `checkpoint_bytes`, `interrupt_count`

- Alert: run stuck in interrupt > SLA

## Tradeoffs (explicit)

| Option | Upside | Downside |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Central LiteLLM proxy | Uniform logs, budgets, fallbacks | Single point of failure; needs HA |
| Per-service API keys | Team velocity | No cost attribution; secret sprawl |

| --- | --- | --- |
| Adopt now | … | Why Ingest → gateway (caching on) → extract → validate → LangGraph → stage DB is in scope this month |

- How do you allocate model budget per team without shared API keys?
- When is fallback worse than failing fast?

lab_practice.markdown:
## Lab & Practice

**DE lens:** Ship a measurable artifact in your portfolio repo; prove with tests or benchmarks.

### Real-world placement

After single-model extraction works, production needs failover—not a 3am pages for 429s.

### What you implement

Create `gateway/gateway.py` wrapping `litellm.completion` with Tenacity retries on HTTP 429 (exponential backoff, max 3), logging `prompt_hash` (sha256 of system+user), `model`, tokens, and `latency_ms` to `logs/usage.jsonl`.

### Expected outcome

README shows one forced failure switching to fallback successfully.

### Starter code (adapt paths)

```python
# gateway/gateway.py
import hashlib
import json
import time
from tenacity import retry, retry_if_exception, stop_after_attempt, wait_exponential
from litellm import completion
from litellm.exceptions import RateLimitError

def _prompt_hash(messages: list[dict]) -> str:
    blob = json.dumps(messages, sort_keys=True).encode()
    return hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest()[:16]

@retry(
    retry=retry_if_exception(lambda e: isinstance(e, RateLimitError)),
    wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=1, min=1, max=30),
    stop=stop_after_attempt(3),
)
def complete(job_id: str, messages: list[dict]) -> dict:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    resp = completion(model="gpt-4o-mini", messages=messages, metadata={"job_id": job_id})
    row = {
        "job_id": job_id,
        "prompt_hash": _prompt_hash(messages),
        "model": resp.model,
        "prompt_tokens": resp.usage.prompt_tokens,
        "completion_tokens": resp.usage.completion_tokens,
        "latency_ms": int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000),
    }
    with open("logs/usage.jsonl", "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
    return row
```

**Primary source:** [LiteLLM proxy server](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/simple_proxy)

# LiteLLM proxy server

> **Platform depth** — engineering judgment: tradeoffs, metrics, failures, interviews. Read **Study guide** first if you have not done the checklist.

## Platform narrative (this topic)

LiteLLM is the **control plane** for model routing: budgets, fallbacks, and uniform logging. Design for **multi-tenant** use even in a solo repo—per-request metadata (job_id, pipeline, tenant) must flow into logs for cost chargeback. Alert on fallback rate spikes; they often indicate quality or availability regression, not healthy resilience.

## How this topic fits the month’s architecture

- Health checks and LiteLLM sidecar
- Reproducible deploy and rollback (DEPLOY.md)
- Smoke eval + policy after deploy
- Twelve-factor agents
- docs/adding-a-tool.md (peer-reviewable)

## Primary source focus

- Reliable completions
- Fallbacks
- Timeouts

## Failure modes to design for

- Fallback model serves 100% of traffic silently—quality drifts undetected.
- 429 storms without client-side backoff take down the worker pool.
- Prompt+response logged with PII for debugging.

## Metrics and alerts

- `usd_per_request_p99`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `latency_ms_p99`

- Alert: fallback_rate > 5% over 15m

- Alert: validation_error_rate spike vs 7d baseline

## Tradeoffs (explicit)

| Option | Upside | Downside |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Central LiteLLM proxy | Uniform logs, budgets, fallbacks | Single point of failure; needs HA |
| Per-service API keys | Team velocity | No cost attribution; secret sprawl |

## Decision record (fill before you ship)

| Stance | Your choice | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adopt now | … | Why LiteLLM proxy server is in scope this month |
| Experiment | … | What you will measure in two weeks |
| Defer | … | What risk you accept by waiting |

- Draw a box diagram: where does **LiteLLM proxy server** sit between data landing and warehouse load?
- What is your rollback plan if a model upgrade drops golden-set pass rate by 5%?
- How do you prove schema validity ≠ semantic correctness with one example?
- How do you allocate model budget per team without shared API keys?
- When is fallback worse than failing fast?

README shows one forced failure switching to fallback successfully.

## Production notes (still plain English)

Before changing models or prompts in production, re-check the course **prove pack** and golden-set metrics (cost, latency, valid JSON %).

Re-read rollout and failure-mode sections with gateway metrics and golden-set labels open. Staff reviewers expect explicit tradeoffs on cost, latency, schema strictness, and audit—not a lecture recap.

> **Platform depth** — engineering judgment: tradeoffs, metrics, failures, interviews. Read **Study guide** first if you have not done the checklist.

## Platform narrative (this topic)

Evals are **regression tests for non-deterministic components**. Tier metrics: schema pass rate, task success on golden set, and cost/latency envelopes. Advanced teams block release on **composite** gates, not a single accuracy number.

## How this topic fits the month’s architecture

- Smoke eval + policy after deploy
- Health checks and LiteLLM sidecar
- Reproducible deploy and rollback (DEPLOY.md)
- Twelve-factor agents
- docs/adding-a-tool.md (peer-reviewable)

## Failure modes to design for

- URL points to private repo or non-reproducible demo.
- README metric cannot be recomputed from committed commands.

## Metrics and alerts

- Reviewer time-to-reproduce (target < 10 min)

- CI badge or metric visible in README

## Tradeoffs (explicit)

- **Build vs buy:** API model + gateway before self-hosting weights.
- **Strict schema vs fuzzy parsing:** always strict at the boundary; relax only inside trusted zones.

## Decision record (fill before you ship)

| Stance | Your choice | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Experiment | … | What you will measure in two weeks |

lab_practice.markdown:
## Lab & Practice

**DE lens:** Ship a measurable artifact in your portfolio repo; prove with tests or benchmarks.

### Real-world placement

After single-model extraction works, production needs failover—not a 3am pages for 429s.

### What you implement

Create `gateway/gateway.py` wrapping `litellm.completion` with Tenacity retries on HTTP 429 (exponential backoff, max 3), logging `prompt_hash` (sha256 of system+user), `model`, tokens, and `latency_ms` to `logs/usage.jsonl`.

### Expected outcome

README shows one forced failure switching to fallback successfully.

### Starter code (adapt paths)

```python
# gateway/gateway.py
import hashlib
import json
import time
from tenacity import retry, retry_if_exception, stop_after_attempt, wait_exponential
from litellm import completion
from litellm.exceptions import RateLimitError

def _prompt_hash(messages: list[dict]) -> str:
    blob = json.dumps(messages, sort_keys=True).encode()
    return hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest()[:16]

@retry(
    retry=retry_if_exception(lambda e: isinstance(e, RateLimitError)),
    wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=1, min=1, max=30),
    stop=stop_after_attempt(3),
)
def complete(job_id: str, messages: list[dict]) -> dict:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    resp = completion(model="gpt-4o-mini", messages=messages, metadata={"job_id": job_id})
    row = {
        "job_id": job_id,
        "prompt_hash": _prompt_hash(messages),
        "model": resp.model,
        "prompt_tokens": resp.usage.prompt_tokens,
        "completion_tokens": resp.usage.completion_tokens,
        "latency_ms": int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000),
    }
    with open("logs/usage.jsonl", "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
    return row
```

**Primary source:** [**vLLM** — docs · local model behind LiteLLM](https://docs.vllm.ai/)

- **LLM gateway** — Central entry for models: auth, routing, budgets, logging, fallbacks. _DE angle:_ Kong/Apigee-style layer before downstream services.

- **Audit log** — Append-only record of who invoked which tool with what outcome. _DE angle:_ CloudTrail / data access logs for compliance.
- **Golden set** — Fixed labeled examples (input → expected output) used to score changes. _DE angle:_ Fixture tables in dbt tests or regression datasets.
- **RAG** — Retrieval-augmented generation: fetch relevant docs, then answer with the model. _DE angle:_ Join to a reference table before computing a metric.
- **Embedding** — Vector representation of text used for similarity search. _DE angle:_ Feature vector for fuzzy matching instead of exact keys.
- **Tool schema** — JSON schema describing parameters an agent tool accepts. _DE angle:_ API request body contract.
- **MCP** — Model Context Protocol—standard way to expose tools and resources to models. _DE angle:_ Internal tool catalog + OpenAPI for agents.
- **Sampling** — How the model picks the next token (temperature, top-p). _DE angle:_ Random seed / tie-break policy—lower temperature = more deterministic.
- **Agent** — System that plans steps and calls tools; not just one LLM prompt. _DE angle:_ Orchestrated micro-jobs with side effects—not a single SQL statement.
- **Eval harness** — Scripts/CI that run the golden set and report metrics on every change. _DE angle:_ pytest + data diff job in CI.
- **LLM gateway** — Central entry for models: auth, routing, budgets, logging, fallbacks. _DE angle:_ Kong/Apigee-style layer before downstream services.
- **Structured output** — Forcing LLM responses into a schema (JSON/Pydantic) instead of free text. _DE angle:_ Contract-first API response types and schema enforcement.

10.capstone_product_brief_markdown:
# Capstone product brief (Course 10)

Use this as the **scope contract** for integration month. Wire existing modules; do not add new frameworks until the demo runs.

## Product name

**OpsLedger AI** — internal platform for turning messy operational text (logs, tickets, runbook snippets) into typed records, with human approval on risky rows.

## Personas

| Persona | Need |
| --- | --- |
| **Platform engineer (you)** | One repo, one demo, prove artifacts for gateway, eval CI, policy, traces |
| **On-call analyst** | Search past incidents; never get a write tool without policy allow |
| **Reviewer / staff engineer** | Reproduce alpha in <10 minutes from README |

## User stories (must demo)

1. **Ingest** — Upload or point at synthetic `data/corpus/`; chunks land with `doc_id`, `chunk_id`, `source_page`.
2. **Extract** — CLI or API call returns Pydantic-validated `LogEvent` rows; invalid rows quarantined.
3. **HITL** — Force a validation failure; LangGraph interrupts; operator fixes state; run resumes.
4. **Ask + retrieve** — One labeled question hits hybrid retrieval; answer cites chunk ids (no mystery prose).

## Synthetic dataset (public only)

- `data/corpus/` — 10–20 markdown or JSON log files (fabricated or public 10-K excerpts).
- `data/golden/` — ≥30 labeled extraction rows (Course 0/7 bars).
- `benchmarks/queries.jsonl` — ≥15 Q/A pairs with `expected_chunk_ids` for recall@k (Course 4).

## SLO table (write real numbers in README)

| SLO | Target (alpha) | How you measure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Golden schema pass rate | ≥90% on n≥30 | `evals/run.py` |
| P95 extract latency | <8s per row (API path) | LiteLLM usage JSONL |
| Eval CI | Blocks merge on regression | GitHub Actions link |
| Policy | Deny `write_*` for role `analyst` | `opa test` output |
| Trace | One `run_id` across gateway + graph | Redacted Langfuse/OTel sample |

## Course 10 lesson buckets

| Bucket | Intent |
| --- | --- |
| **Wire** | Connect gateway, graph, MCP read tools, retrieval, eval hook |
| **Caching evidence** | Stable system prefix; README table TTFT + cached tokens (≥10 requests) |
| **Demo** | One command: `docker compose up` or `make demo` — happy path + one HITL fail path |

## Non-goals for alpha

- Multi-tenant billing, fine-tuned weights, or net-new RAG research
- Production customer data in any external API
